## Plan

**Blocking dependence:** The evidence shows exactly one loop-carried blocker for the `i`-loop: a RAW on `v` where line 20 (`v[jv[i]] = u[ku[i]]*d[i]+c[i]`) writes a value that a *later* iteration's line 19 (`u[ju[i]] += v[kv[i]]*c[i]`) reads. That's a genuine value-in-transit, so it can't be deleted, only moved: the write side has to fully finish before the read side starts — matching the digest's own guidance ("the loop holding line 20 has to run completely before the loop holding line 19 runs").

The other listed items are not blockers for this loop:
- `u`'s RAW is self-contained in line 19's own `+=` (no cross-iteration RAW on `u` was ever reported), so `u[ku[i]]` read in line 20 never observes a same-rep update from line 19 — it's effectively constant for the whole `i`-loop, safe to read before line 19 has run at all.
- `d`'s RAW is carried by the outer `nl` loop (via `pb_mix`), not the `i` loop; that ordering is already preserved since `pb_mix(nl)` still runs after both inner loops, in order.

**Fix (loop fission):** split the fused loop into two full passes over `i` (same bounds, `1 .. LEN_1D-1`), keeping `nl`'s sequential order and `pb_mix(nl)` after both:
1. First pass: only line 20 (`v[jv[i]] = u[ku[i]]*d[i]+c[i]`) — reads only `u`,`d`,`c` (none written in this pass), so all iterations are independent → Do-All.
2. Second pass: only line 19 (`u[ju[i]] += v[kv[i]]*c[i]`) — now reads the fully-completed `v` from pass 1 (exactly the value the original sequential run would have produced by the time it reached line 19, since no line-20 write past that point could still affect it under the no-cross-alias evidence), and writes to `u` — independent per the evidence.

No new buffers needed since `v` and `u` are already the full arrays; nothing grows with input size beyond the existing O(n) work (just two O(n) passes instead of one, a constant factor).The rewrite splits the fused `i`-loop (lines 18–21) into two sequential full-range passes, both still inside the unchanged `nl` loop and before `pb_mix(nl)`:

1. `v[jv[i]] = u[ku[i]] * d[i] + c[i];` over all `i` — reads only inputs that aren't written anywhere in this pass, so it's independent across `i`.
2. `u[ju[i]] += v[kv[i]] * c[i];` over all `i` — runs only after pass 1 fully completes, so it sees the same `v` values the original sequential code would have produced by that point, and doesn't write anything pass 1 depends on.
